reason: The text explicitly demonstrates Yahweh's compassion and protective stance toward the Hebrew people. When the Israelites cry out in their oppression under Egypt, Yahweh hears their groaning, remembers His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and declares His intention to deliver them from bondage. God promises: 'I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians, and I will deliver you from their bondage, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm.' God further promises to take them as His people and bring them to Canaan. The plagues described are directed against Egypt and Pharaoh, not against the Hebrew people, serving as the means to force their liberation. Throughout, Yahweh is portrayed as responsive to Israel's suffering and actively working for their redemption.
